question: Can trainable continuous prompt embeddings, added to discrete prompts, stabilise and improve NLU performance of pretrained language models (frozen or tuned)?
hypothesis: Continuous prompts add learnability to the input that can offset the effect of small changes in discrete prompts, improving training stability and performance.
contributions: P-Tuning: trainable continuous prompt embeddings concatenated with discrete prompts, produced through a prompt encoder (LSTM or MLP)
Gains on LAMA knowledge probing (frozen LM) and SuperGLUE (tuned LM, fully-supervised and few-shot)
Reduced performance gap between different discrete prompts

method.summary: A template mixes discrete prompt tokens and trainable pseudo-token embeddings [P_i]; a lightweight prompt encoder f (LSTM, MLP or identity) maps them to input vectors h_i, and the embeddings are updated by backpropagation on the task loss. The LM is either frozen (LAMA) or jointly tuned (SuperGLUE).
method.task: Knowledge probing (LAMA cloze) and SuperGLUE NLU classification, fully-supervised and few-shot

datasets.name: LAMA-TREx (LAMA-34k)
datasets.split: train/dev/test constructed following Shin et al. (2020)
datasets.preprocessing: answers single-token; covers all BERT vocabularies

datasets.name: LAMA-29k
datasets.split: train/dev/test constructed following Shin et al. (2020)
datasets.source: subset of LAMA covering intersection of GPT and BERT vocabularies

datasets.name: SuperGLUE (7 of 8 tasks: BoolQ, MultiRC, CB, RTE, WiC, COPA, WSC)
datasets.split: development set reported; ReCoRD excluded as it has no discrete prompts

datasets.name: FewGLUE
datasets.split: data splits built following FewNLU (Zheng et al. 2021), random splits, model selection on small labeled set

models.name: P-tuning prompt encoder
models.architecture: LSTM, MLP or identity (EMB) mapping f: P_i -> h_i

other.LAMA_template_bidirectional: (3, sub, org_prompt, 3, obj, 3): 3 continuous tokens at each position

training.objective: task loss (cloze / classification) backpropagated into continuous prompt embeddings; LM frozen on LAMA, jointly optimised with prompts on SuperGLUE
training.lr: LAMA: 1e-5; fully-supervised SuperGLUE: searched {1e-5, 2e-5, 3e-5}; few-shot: searched {1e-5, 2e-5}
training.steps: few-shot: max training steps searched {250, 500}, evaluation frequency {0.02, 0.04}
training.epochs: 20 for small datasets (COPA, WSC, CB, RTE); 10 for WiC, BoolQ, MultiRC; early stopping
training.seeds: few-shot: each result averaged over 4 runs with different data splits

other.LAMA_prompt_positions: number of prompt tokens and positions selected on development sets

inference.decoding: cloze: predict [MASK] token for bidirectional LMs; for GPT use network output just before the target position
inference.samples: few-shot: 4 runs with different data splits
inference.prompting: continuous prompts concatenated with original discrete (manual LAMA / PET) prompts

metrics.name: Precision@1
metrics.definition: LAMA cloze top-1 accuracy of predicted tail entity

metrics.name: SuperGLUE task metrics
metrics.definition: as in Wang et al. 2019 (Acc., F1, F1a, EM); Avg across tasks

metrics.name: Std over patterns
metrics.definition: standard deviation of results across different discrete prompt patterns, used as a stability measure

eval.protocol: Fully-supervised: development set for hyper-parameter and model selection. Few-shot: FewNLU procedure with random data splits and model selection on a small labeled set; same hyper-parameter search space for PET and P-tuning.

results.setup: LAMA-34k, BERT-large with P-tuning vs best discrete baseline, frozen LM

limits: Fully-supervised SuperGLUE (Table 4) reports single numbers with no variance; the authors concede the gap between discrete prompts is not large and training is stable even without P-Tuning there (Table 2).
Gains over PET in few-shot average are about 1 point while per-task std is several points; P-tuning loses on RTE.
ReCoRD excluded because it has no discrete prompts; P-tuning not directly applicable.
Compute, hardware, seeds for fully-supervised runs, prompt encoder size and number of continuous tokens per SuperGLUE task are not stated; patterns are chosen per task by search.

Only NLU with small encoder or GPT-2 scale models (and MegatronLM 11B on LAMA); no generation tasks or modern LLMs. Prompt Tuning (Lester et al. 2021) is compared on ALBERT, where it is weak; Lester et al. says it works with large models.
LAMA gains mix learned prompts with training data on relation triples, so improved P@1 partly measures fitting, not elicited pretrained knowledge (not discussed by authors).
